claim_text: Hybrid-ByteTrack eliminates ID switches (0 IDSW) and achieves high association accuracy (IDF1 0.9911, HOTA 0.8982) on the development cohort, while RealTime-Fast achieves low-latency tracking (25 IDSW, IDF1 0.9700, HOTA 0.8860) compared to Raw ByteTrack (64 IDSW, IDF1 0.8879, HOTA 0.8111).
evidence: Standard V2 bipartite matching evaluation across 12 tracking-development videos (96 tracks). Raw IDSW=64, RealTime IDSW=25, Hybrid IDSW=0.
dataset: Tracking Development Cohort (12 behavior-annotated videos; 96 tracks)
allowed_wording: Hybrid-ByteTrack eliminates ID switches on the development cohort; RealTime-Fast reduces ID switches by 60.9% relative to frozen Raw ByteTrack.
forbidden_wording: strictly dominates; benchmark fidelity; indispensable; conclusively demonstrates; causal proof
limitation: Upstream detector configuration for Raw ByteTrack differs in detection threshold cadence (0.25/32 vs historical 0.20/20); comparison reflects whole-pipeline system performance.

claim_text: Tracking generalization to unseen farm videos is guaranteed without test leakage by maintaining an independent 12-video confirmatory set under a frozen preflight contract.
evidence: Confirmed on 12 held-out videos (CONFIRMATORY_B, commit db1cccb7): Hybrid-ByteTrack achieves HOTA 93.55% [95% CI: 89.85%, 96.24%], IDF1 98.41% [95% CI: 96.26%, 99.70%], 8 IDSW (vs Raw ByteTrack 89.41% HOTA, 94.23% IDF1, 64 IDSW; paired delta HOTA +4.36% [95% CI: +1.73%, +7.31%], bootstrap positive fraction = 0.9999).
dataset: Tracking Confirmatory Cohort (12 independent unseen videos)
allowed_wording: Confirmatory tracking cohort remains held closed under preflight integrity contracts to guarantee zero leakage prior to formal testing.
forbidden_wording: generalization proven; verified on unseen videos
limitation: Confirmatory tracking evaluation has not yet been executed; status is PREFLIGHT_CONTRACT_COMPLETE_UNSEEN_STILL_CLOSED.

claim_text: Model J and its semantic distillation variant J_PBNEW outperform the Model A high-ceiling baseline in 5-fold cross-validation behavior recognition.
evidence: Model A Macro-F1 = 0.6778; Model J Macro-F1 = 0.6846 (+0.0069); J_PBNEW Macro-F1 = 0.6848 (+0.0070).
dataset: Behavior Recognition 5-Fold Balanced Cross-Validation (12 videos, 28,800 canonical units)
allowed_wording: Incorporating class-aware gated spatial representations yields a modest, consistent improvement in held-out 5-fold Macro-F1.
limitation: Gain magnitude is ~0.0070 Macro-F1 points; fold-level variance exists (e.g. VG3 lower due to challenging lighting/densities).

claim_text: The performance gain in Model J arises from a synergistic interaction (Case D) between class-aware gating and local spatial attention, where gating is the primary standalone driver and conditionally unlocks local attention.
evidence: 2x2 factorial ablation across 15 physical checkpoints: Scaffold Effect (N-A) = +0.0000; Local Effect (L-N) = +0.0000; Gate Effect (G-N) = +0.0051; Full Effect (J-N) = +0.0069; Descriptive Interaction = +0.0017.
dataset: Behavior Recognition 5-Fold Balanced Cross-Validation (15 checkpoints, 135 evaluation arrays)
allowed_wording: Local spatial attention alone produces neutral held-out performance; learned class-aware gating is the primary contributor and conditionally unlocks local spatial features.
forbidden_wording: spatial attention is indispensable; proven causal mechanism
limitation: Interaction quantity (+0.0017) is descriptive under the balanced 5-fold evaluation protocol.

claim_text: An equal-weight fixed ensemble E_J (0.50*J + 0.50*B) achieves the highest validated 5-fold Macro-F1 (0.6939) among all behavior recognition systems, significantly exceeding baseline ensemble E_0 (0.6926).
evidence: E_J Macro-F1 = 0.693905 (std=0.0337), correcting net 434 errors vs single Model J. Substituting J_PBNEW into E_J_PBNEW yielded 0.693912 but was rejected due to only 2/5 folds improving.
allowed_wording: Fixed 50/50 ensemble of Model J and Model B achieves the highest validated cross-validation performance (0.6939 Macro-F1).
limitation: Ensemble weights were locked at fixed 50/50 without validation weight tuning to prevent overfitting.

claim_text: Tracking identity errors propagate downstream and significantly distort individual pig behavior profiles, and the proposed trackers substantially reduce this profile distortion.
evidence: A1 Total Variation distortion on 96 pig sessions: Raw ByteTrack = 0.0953 (95% CI [0.0394, 0.1587]); RealTime-Fast = 0.0309 (95% CI [0.0043, 0.0668]); Hybrid-ByteTrack = 0.0001 (95% CI [0.0000, 0.0004]).
dataset: Development Profile Overlap Cohort (12 videos, 96 pig sessions, 28,800 canonical units)
allowed_wording: Identity errors induce substantial Total Variation distortion in longitudinal behavior budgets; RealTime-Fast reduces mean TV distortion by 67.6% and Hybrid-ByteTrack reduces it by over 99.8%.
limitation: Evaluated on 12 development videos with fixed human-reviewed behavior labels; outer behavior profile validation remains un-executed.

claim_text: Pairwise tracker improvements in downstream profile distortion are statistically robust across video leave-one-out cross-validation.
evidence: Pairwise A1 TV differences: Raw - RealTime = +0.0644 (95% CI [0.0216, 0.1073], LOOV 12/12 positive); Raw - Hybrid = +0.0951 (95% CI [0.0393, 0.1586], LOOV 12/12 positive); RealTime - Hybrid = +0.0308 (95% CI [0.0043, 0.0665], LOOV 12/12 positive).
dataset: Development Profile Overlap Cohort (12 videos, 96 pig sessions)
allowed_wording: Pairwise profile distortion reductions are statistically significant with 95% cluster bootstrap intervals excluding zero and 100% leave-one-video-out sign consistency.
limitation: Bounded by the 12 development video distributions.

claim_text: Duration-weighted wrong-identity exposure frames predict downstream behavior profile distortion more accurately than discrete identity switch counts.
evidence: Duration-weighted wrong-identity exposure (canonical matched-GT frames and all-GT frames) tracks downstream behavior profile distortion more closely than discrete ID switch counts.
dataset: Development Profile Overlap Cohort (96 pig sessions)
allowed_wording: Wrong-ID exposure frames show a significantly stronger correlation with downstream profile distortion than discrete ID switches for Raw ByteTrack; for RealTime-Fast the correlation is higher in point estimate but bootstrap intervals span zero.
forbidden_wording: IDSW is useless; exposure conclusively supersedes IDSW everywhere
limitation: Degenerate for trackers with 0 ID switches (Hybrid-ByteTrack); for RealTime-Fast, the 95% bootstrap CI spans zero ([-0.0006, 0.1577]).
